title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit Low (Extended)
shortDescription: High-pressure fuel pump regulator solenoid command low — actual rail pressure undershoots target.
fullDescription: High-pressure fuel pump regulator solenoid command low — actual rail pressure undershoots target. On modern direct-injection systems the high-pressure side runs between 50 and 350 bar, so even a small leak, a worn HPFP cam follower, a sticking regulator solenoid, or noise on the rail-pressure sensor will set this code. The PCM will usually fall back to a low-pressure limp strategy until the underlying issue is corrected.
safetyImpact: Loss of high-pressure fuel control can cause stalling, hard starting, or sudden power loss — potentially unsafe in traffic.

causes.cause: Failed high-pressure fuel pump (cam follower wear)
Failed or contaminated rail pressure sensor
Stuck or seized fuel pressure regulator solenoid
Wiring open/short on regulator or sensor circuit
Low-pressure (lift) pump weak — starves HPFP
Fuel injector internal leak

fixSteps.title: Read live rail pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use a capable scan tool to compare commanded vs actual fuel rail pressure during cranking and at idle. A persistent gap > 15% is the key diagnostic clue.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors and harness
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the rail pressure sensor and HPFP regulator connector. Look for fuel contamination, bent pins, and chafed wiring along the engine harness.

fixSteps.title: Test low-pressure supply
fixSteps.instruction: Tee a gauge into the low-pressure supply line. Spec is typically 4-6 bar at idle. Replace the in-tank pump if undersupplied.

fixSteps.title: Replace HPFP / regulator
fixSteps.instruction: If supply is good and the sensor checks out, remove the high-pressure fuel pump and inspect the cam follower. Replace pump and follower as a set on BMW/VW; replace integrated regulator solenoid where serviced separately.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving?
faq.a: Briefly to a shop yes, but a high-pressure fuel leak is a fire hazard — if you smell fuel, stop and tow.

faq.q: Can a dirty fuel filter cause this?
faq.a: Yes — a clogged filter starves the HPFP. Always replace the filter as part of a high-pressure fuel diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors and harness
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the rail pressure sensor and HPFP regulator connector. Look for fuel contamination, bent pins, and chafed wiring along the engine harness.

fixSteps.title: Test low-pressure supply
fixSteps.instruction: Tee a gauge into the low-pressure supply line. Spec is typically 4-6 bar at idle. Replace the in-tank pump if undersupplied.

fixSteps.title: Replace HPFP / regulator
fixSteps.instruction: If supply is good and the sensor checks out, remove the high-pressure fuel pump and inspect the cam follower. Replace pump and follower as a set on BMW/VW; replace integrated regulator solenoid where serviced separately.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving?
faq.a: Briefly to a shop yes, but a high-pressure fuel leak is a fire hazard — if you smell fuel, stop and tow.

faq.q: Can a dirty fuel filter cause this?
faq.a: Yes — a clogged filter starves the HPFP. Always replace the filter as part of a high-pressure fuel diagnosis.
